text:
The highlight clip is complete: a continuous 60-second cut (0–60s of the source) that opens on the group's arrival at the cliff edge — the banter, name-checks, and "Meeting at the bottom of this cliff... I'll try to follow if I don't" setup — carries through the dramatic "Oh, God!" reaction at 30s (confirmed in the frame check: skiers mid-descent on the slope, a strong action beat), and closes on the "You okay? I'll try to follow you later" exchange, ending cleanly on a finished sentence at the 60s mark. No cut lands mid-word or mid-sentence anywhere in the span — the first line ("Whoo!") starts the clip and the last line ("...follow you later.") finishes exactly as the clip ends.

I kept this as one unbroken take rather than a stitched compilation: the material with real narrative variety (intro, plan, the "Oh God" moment, the check-in) all sits inside this first minute, while everything past ~60s in the source is the same "I'll try to follow you later" line repeating for the rest of the 9-minute recording — not usable highlight material to cut in against. A single continuous minute also avoids any jarring internal cuts on POV action footage where a mid-shot cut would be more noticeable than on a static talking-head frame.

Visually reviewed at 31s, 40s, and 59.5s — the picture holds up throughout (clear ski-slope action, no dead frames or glitches at the cut points). The edit is ready as a 60-second highlight; I have not exported it, since that wasn't requested — say the word and I'll run the export.
